text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- LAND TAX APPROVED, LAND PRICES LIKELY TO DROP FURTHER

Brazil's federal government on Wednesday got congressional approval of a new land tax which will levy a 20 percent charge on unused properties of more than 5,000 hectares. With the new tax approved, land prices, which have been falling in the last two years, are likely to drop further.
-- GERDAU TO SELL PART OF PAINS

Gerdau group decided to sell part of its steel mill Siderurgica Pains in Minas Gerais state to maintain the control of the company. The option was one of the three offered to Gerdau group by the government's anti-trust body investigating the legality of the conglomerate's acquisition of Pains in February last year.
-- PETROBRAS, DOW AND YPF TOGETHER IN GASLINE
Dow Chemical, Brazil's Petrobras and Argentina's YPF are holding talks to build a $400 million gas pipeline in Argentina.
-- APPROVED DEAL MAKING BANESPA A FEDERAL BANK
Sao Paulo state's Legislative Assembly approved late Wednesday a deal allowing Sao Paulo state bank Banespa to be taken over by the federal government.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GUERRILLAS HOLD HOSTAGES IN PERU

A group of 23 guerrillas stormed the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima and seized more than 200 hostages. At least 15 ambassadors are in the hands of the rebels, including the Brazilian ambassador Carlos Luiz Coutinho Perez and a brother of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori.
-- WORKER KILLS THREE, HURTS TWO AND COMMITS SUICIDE AT SABESP
An office worker shot dead three colleagues, hurt two men and then turned the gun on himself on Wednesday at Sao Paulo's state sewage company Sabesp.
O GLOBO
-- MARCELLO AND CONDE FIGHT FOR ICMS TAX

A bill proposed by Rio de Janeiro state governor Marcello Alencar altering the distribution of the ICMS tax has raised protests from Rio de Janeiro city mayor Cesar Maia and the elected mayor Luiz Paulo Conde.
-- RONALDINHO MAY EARN AS A NBA STAR

In addition to making $3.8 million a year at Spanish club Barcelona, striker Ronaldinho may earn like a NBA star. The main Spain's sweet company wants Ronaldinho to be the model of its advertising campaign.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
